text: Remove the nonlinear context residual and retain only the additive user, video, tab, hour, and weekday terms.
rationale: Experiment 2 improved only modestly over experiment 1, while experiment 3's stronger residual regularization slightly reduced primary, suggesting the residual may add variance rather than robust ranking signal. This is a clean rollback test against the strongest measured parent.
exact_ablation: Replace the parent model's additive-plus-32-unit-ReLU context residual with the parent additive scorer only; keep all five fields, BCE, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and stopping rule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely decrease by 0.0002 to 0.0015 because the residual may capture some context nonlinearity; it could be flat or slightly positive if residual overfitting is harmful.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely decrease by 0.0002 to 0.0012, with possible improvement if noisy residual scores currently perturb the top five.

text: Add dropout to the nonlinear request-context residual while preserving its learned embeddings and additive ID terms.
rationale: The parent residual raised GAUC from 0.668912 to 0.669129 and nDCG@5 from 0.536958 to 0.537206, but stronger L2 in experiment 3 did not improve primary. Dropout tests a different variance-control mechanism without changing the feature family.
exact_ablation: Apply dropout rate 0.10 to the hidden representation of the existing 32-unit context residual during training only; keep inference deterministic and leave features, loss, optimizer, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely increase by 0.0001 to 0.0008 if the residual is overfitting; excessive stochasticity could reduce GAUC by up to 0.0005.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely increase by 0.0002 to 0.0010 through more stable top-five ordering, but small-slice volatility may remain.

text: Reduce the context residual capacity from 32 hidden units to 8 hidden units.
rationale: The residual gain over experiment 1 was only 0.000233 primary, and the experiment 3 regularization change slightly regressed. A smaller residual directly tests whether the useful context effect is low-dimensional and whether excess capacity harms generalization.
exact_ablation: Change only the nonlinear context residual hidden width from 32 ReLU units to 8; preserve its embeddings, output head, additive ID terms, BCE, optimizer, and all hyperparameters otherwise.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely flat to +0.0006 as noisy residual degrees of freedom are removed; a loss of up to 0.0004 is possible if the parent uses genuinely complex context effects.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely +0.0001 to +0.0008 from smoother ranking, though reduced capacity could make the effect flat.

text: Add an explicit tab-by-hour categorical interaction to the existing request-context input.
rationale: The request-context group was the only screened feature group with positive temporal primary lift, while tab 8 and tab 3 have extremely weak top-five metrics. An explicit interaction may capture presentation-time effects that the current residual does not reliably learn.
exact_ablation: Add one train-vocabulary categorical field representing the pair (tab,hour), with an unknown bucket; keep the original fields, residual architecture, BCE, optimizer, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely increase by 0.0002 to 0.0010 if context effects differ by tab; sparse combinations could instead reduce GAUC by up to 0.0005.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely increase by 0.0004 to 0.0015, especially on weak tab slices, with top-five regression risk for rare interaction values.

text: Replace categorical hour with a compact cyclic hour representation in the context residual.
rationale: Hour slices are weak and irregular, including GAUC 0.5242 at hour 3 and 0.5917 at hour 8, so independent hour embeddings may not generalize across adjacent times. A cyclic representation tests whether smooth daily structure improves context ranking.
exact_ablation: Replace only the categorical hour input to the nonlinear residual with two training-normalized numeric features sin(2π hour/24) and cos(2π hour/24); retain the categorical hour additive term, all other fields, loss, optimizer, and schedule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely increase by 0.0001 to 0.0008 if adjacent hours share behavior; it may decrease by 0.0005 if hour effects are discontinuous.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely increase by 0.0002 to 0.0010 through smoother ordering across hours, but gains may be negligible in sparse slices.

text: Remove weekday from the request-context fields while retaining tab and hour.
rationale: The measured request-context evidence supports the group overall but does not identify which field drives the gain. Weekday has only seven values and may introduce unstable calendar-specific corrections; this single-field ablation isolates its contribution.
exact_ablation: Delete only the weekday feature from the input and its residual embedding; keep user ID, video ID, tab, hour, residual architecture, BCE, optimizer, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely change by -0.0004 to +0.0002; weekday may provide weak signal but can also add noise.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely change by -0.0005 to +0.0003, with no expected material effect if weekday does not reorder candidates within users.

text: Remove tab from the request-context fields while retaining hour and weekday.
rationale: Tab-specific slices are the weakest diagnostics, including tab 8 GAUC 0.3519 and nDCG@5 0.0263, so tab may encode a noisy exposure policy rather than stable preference. Removing it tests whether the apparent group gain is driven by the more general temporal fields.
exact_ablation: Delete only the tab feature from the additive and residual inputs; retain hour, weekday, IDs, residual architecture, BCE, optimizer, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely decrease by 0.0003 to 0.0012 if tab contains useful within-user exposure context; it could increase by up to 0.0004 if tab overfits.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely decrease by 0.0005 to 0.0018 because tab may distinguish top-five exposure regimes, though weak-tab support makes the estimate noisy.

text: Remove hour from the request-context fields while retaining tab and weekday.
rationale: Hour-specific validation slices are consistently below aggregate primary, with particularly weak hour 3 and hour 8 results. This ablation tests whether hour is a harmful shortcut under temporal drift despite the positive aggregate request-context screen.
exact_ablation: Delete only the hour feature from the additive and residual inputs; retain tab, weekday, IDs, residual architecture, BCE, optimizer, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely decrease by 0.0002 to 0.0010 if hour captures real availability patterns; it could be flat or improve by up to 0.0005 under temporal drift.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely decrease by 0.0003 to 0.0014 if hour helps top-five ordering, with a plausible small improvement if hour corrections are unstable.

text: Train the parent model with a within-user pairwise ranking loss instead of BCE.
rationale: The official objective is within-user ordering, while the current model uses BCE. Experiment 2 has stronger GAUC than nDCG@5 in absolute terms, so a ranking-aligned loss may improve ordering, although pair construction and small candidate groups create implementation risk.
exact_ablation: Replace BCE training with unweighted RankNet over positive-negative pairs formed only within each user; retain the exact parent features, residual architecture, optimizer, learning rate, and checkpoint rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely increase by 0.0003 to 0.0015 because the loss directly optimizes positive-negative ordering; sparse users may cause a decrease of up to 0.0008.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely increase by 0.0005 to 0.0020 because top-ranked positives receive direct pairwise pressure, but pair sampling can make top-five results volatile.

text: Use a top-five-weighted within-user pairwise loss instead of BCE.
rationale: Experiment 2 reaches nDCG@5 0.537206 while the official GAUC is 0.669129, indicating room to target top-of-list quality separately. A pairwise loss weighted toward high predicted ranks is materially different from standard BCE and tests the nDCG weakness directly.
exact_ablation: Replace BCE with a within-user pairwise logistic loss whose pair weight is 1 for pairs involving the current predicted top five and 0.25 otherwise; keep features, architecture, optimizer, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely flat to +0.0008; concentrating on top ranks could reduce broad ordering and lower GAUC by up to 0.0010.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely increase by 0.0007 to 0.0025 if top-five mistakes are corrected, with high variance from changing predicted pair membership.

text: Use gradient clipping during training for the parent context-residual model.
rationale: The nonlinear residual changes validation score variance and its stronger-regularization variant has a slightly worse primary, suggesting optimization instability may contribute. Gradient clipping changes training dynamics without changing the scoring function or permitted inputs.
exact_ablation: Clip the global minibatch gradient norm to 1.0 immediately before every parameter update; keep the parent model, features, BCE, optimizer, learning rate, and stopping rule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely increase by 0.0001 to 0.0007 if occasional large updates harm generalization; clipping could reduce GAUC by up to 0.0004 if updates are already well behaved.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely increase by 0.0002 to 0.0009 through more stable top-five scores, though the aggregate effect may be flat.

text: Replace the residual's separate context embeddings with a single shared embedding table for tab, hour, and weekday values.
rationale: The context fields are low-cardinality, yet the parent uses three independent embedding tables and a nonlinear head. Parameter sharing may regularize sparse context combinations and improve weak tab/hour slices, but it risks erasing field-specific semantics.
exact_ablation: Use one shared 8-dimensional context embedding table with field-specific value offsets for tab, hour, and weekday in the nonlinear residual; leave additive field weights, all features, BCE, optimizer, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely increase by 0.0001 to 0.0009 if shared structure regularizes the residual; semantic interference could reduce GAUC by up to 0.0007.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely increase by 0.0002 to 0.0012 on sparse context values, but top-five gains are uncertain because tab and hour may require different representations.
